purpose: Prepare a bounded non-canonical Hermes advisory review of the landed Launch Ladder planning/spec package, focused on slop risk, authority drift, product primitives, stale source-set risk, operator control, evidence freshness, launch semantics, local-first OpenClaw alignment, Multi-OpenClaw Command Atlas fit, and portability to personal and future client deployments.
source_set_refresh_notes: Launch Ladder planning/spec docs are present in docs/planning/launch_ladder and included as explicit allowed read surfaces.
Refresh this packet before a Hermes advisory run if any allowed source file changes or the Launch Ladder package commit/freshness metadata changes.
Treat this packet as source-set ready for later manual Hermes advisory review only; it does not run Hermes or authorize execution.
review_questions: Does the Launch Ladder planning/spec stay bounded to advisory planning and avoid canonical authority by implication?
Does the package keep the Multi-OpenClaw Command Atlas as a horizon while proving only the v1 Launch Ladder work layer?
Do Launch Ladders clearly replace vague lanes as the operator-facing unit of work without erasing deferred work?
Do route compression, compact buttons, and Parallel Step Bundles preserve stop conditions, evidence, collision boundaries, validation, and authority requirements?
Which product primitives are missing before Launch Ladder can honestly support personal OpenClaw and future client deployments?
Where could source-set drift cause stale or overconfident recommendations?
Does the planning/spec make operator control, evidence freshness, and withheld surfaces explicit enough?
Does the routing/workspace model keep PC/WSL, Mac, Codex Desktop, ChatGPT Projects, Gemini/Hermes advisory, and future client routes explicit and bounded?
Does the security/authority model keep launch-ready separate from launch-authorized and preserve the Hermes advisory-only boundary?
Does the Mac/iOS app build brief keep the first app read-only with no service control, provider/model calls, private data, or canonical authority?
Do the productization profiles separate personal OpenClaw from future client/company deployments without copying private or authority-bearing assumptions wholesale?
Are any launch semantics unsafe because they imply provider execution, live inspection, service/timer changes, queue mutation, or private-data access?
